title: DrunkenAD - Architecture & Flows
subtitle: An interactive map of the PowerShell module, its Active Directory data-store model, operator workflows, validation gates, and release surfaces.

lanes.title: Operator Inputs
lanes.description: Human operators, CSV files, namespace maps, and live-lab wrappers feed the module.

nodes.label: PowerShell operator
nodes.summary: Imports the module, runs Get-Help, previews with -WhatIf, and invokes public commands.

nodes.label: CSV + namespace map
nodes.summary: Rows keyed by SamAccountName plus JSON or hashtable mappings that emit namespaced drink records.

nodes.label: Schema administrator
nodes.summary: Confirms rollback, schema master, forest/domain expectations, then optionally enables drink on the user class.

nodes.label: Live campaign host
nodes.summary: Host-method-neutral wrapper boundary for rollback, workspace access, guest execution, and result collection.

lanes.title: Module Shell
lanes.description: The manifest and deterministic root loader define the public contract.

nodes.label: DrunkenAD.psd1
nodes.summary: Declares version 0.13.2, PowerShell 5.1 support, metadata, and FunctionsToExport parity.

nodes.label: DrunkenAD.psm1
nodes.summary: Small deterministic loader: dot-sources Private then Public scripts and exports the command list.

nodes.label: Get-Help surface
nodes.summary: Comment-based help for every exported command plus about_DrunkenAD as a first-class operator entrypoint.

lanes.title: Public Commands
lanes.description: The supported module API for reading, writing, importing, projecting, and checking readiness.

nodes.label: Get-ADUserDrinkData
nodes.summary: Validates schema presence, resolves exactly one user, and returns all drink values or one literal-prefix namespace.

nodes.label: Set-ADUserDrinkData
nodes.summary: Preferred generic write API. Validates ownership and delegates to a shared writer with one readiness context and a pinned domain controller.

nodes.label: Remove-ADUserDrinkData
nodes.summary: Builds an empty DataMap for one or more prefixes, preserving unrelated values while deleting owned namespaces.

nodes.label: Set-ADUserDrinkProjection
nodes.summary: Resolves the user and source attributes once, retains empty owned prefixes, and reuses the shared private writer and operation context.

nodes.label: Import-ADUserDrinkCsvData
nodes.summary: Preflights local inputs and every usable row before mutation, reuses one readiness context, and reports completed/failed/pending progress on write failure.

nodes.label: Split-DrunkenADCsvField
nodes.summary: Public preview helper for the literal delimiter splitting used by CSV SplitOn mappings.

nodes.label: Schema readiness commands
nodes.summary: Test-ADDrinkAttributeEnabled checks schema presence. Test-ADDrinkAttributeReadyForUserWrite checks whether drink is allowed on user.

nodes.label: Compatibility wrappers
nodes.summary: Older prefixed-data and demo command names remain exported, but new workflows should use the DrinkData and projection APIs.

lanes.title: Private Helpers
lanes.description: Shared internals keep AD lookup, schema checks, prefix maps, projection maps, and CSV mapping consistent.

nodes.label: Core.ps1
nodes.summary: Imports ActiveDirectory, escapes LDAP filter values, resolves exactly one user, normalizes string arrays, and writes optional logs.

nodes.label: WriteOperation.ps1
nodes.summary: Validates schema length bounds and computes prefix-scoped Remove/Add deltas, including case-only changes. Never clears or replaces the entire attribute.

nodes.label: SchemaStatus.ps1
nodes.summary: Preserves explicit endpoints; pins absent servers or domain DNS names to RootDSE's controller. Presence reports do not assess readiness; writes validate rangeUpper and class inheritance.

nodes.label: CsvMapping.ps1
nodes.summary: Validates complete CSV records using the framework parser, normalizes maps and SplitOn values, and emits DataMaps. Blank namespace clearing is opt-in.

nodes.label: ProjectionMap.ps1
nodes.summary: Defines default projection namespaces and converts populated AD attributes into prefix/value maps.

lanes.title: Active Directory
lanes.description: The actual backend stays AD: DrunkenAD only constrains how the multivalued drink attribute is used.

nodes.label: Schema: drink + user
nodes.summary: drink must exist, not be defunct, and be allowed through the user class, its superclasses, or auxiliary classes via optional or mandatory attribute lists.

nodes.label: Resolved AD user
nodes.summary: Every operation uses exact LDAP lookup by one identifier and fails if zero or multiple users match.

nodes.label: drink namespace store
nodes.summary: Each multivalue string is one record: a literal namespace prefix plus a compact payload.

nodes.label: Set-ADUser write
nodes.summary: After ShouldProcess approval, one Set-ADUser call removes then adds owned values on the selected DC. Same-prefix conflicts and cross-DC replication remain external concerns.

lanes.title: Validation & Release
lanes.description: Local checks, CI, docs gates, integration tests, and live campaigns prove different risk levels.

nodes.label: Syntax gate
nodes.summary: Parses tracked PowerShell files before running deeper validation.

nodes.label: Unit + help tests
nodes.summary: Covers owned deltas, case-only writes, stale-read preservation, inherited schema graphs, CSV preflight/progress, trusted discovery failures, release contracts, and help.

nodes.label: Opt-in AD integration
nodes.summary: Opt-in real-directory tests cover CRUD, CSV, projection, case-only updates, and controlled stale reads; cleanup must succeed for the isolated account.

nodes.label: Release readiness gate
nodes.summary: Composes manifest metadata, clean import, export parity, syntax, docs and atlas hygiene, help coverage, and an explicit trusted Pester test allowlist.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions
nodes.summary: PowerShell CI runs with exact Pester 5.7.1 on Ubuntu, macOS, Windows PowerShell Core, and Windows PowerShell 5.1; Documentation CI enforces doc hygiene.

flows.title: Namespace-scoped write
flows.description: The core mutation path: callers own literal prefixes, DrunkenAD preserves everything else.
steps: Caller provides an exact identity and DataMap; local preflight rejects blank or overlapping owned prefixes.
One operation context verifies inherited schema readiness, obtains the actual length bound, and selects a domain controller.
Resolve exactly one user and read drink from that controller.
Partition current values by OrdinalIgnoreCase prefix ownership and validate every desired prefixed value.
Compute case-sensitive Remove/Add deltas for owned values; unrelated values are never sent back as replacements.
After ShouldProcess approval, apply one Set-ADUser call on the same controller; no-op deltas do not write.
PassThru returns a computed snapshot preview, not a fresh read-back. Coordinate same-prefix writers and cross-DC replication externally.

flows.title: Read one user / one namespace
flows.description: Safe read path for inspecting all drink values or a single literal-prefix namespace.
steps: Caller chooses one identity parameter and optionally a Prefix.
Get-ADUserDrinkData validates that drink exists and is not defunct without a write-readiness class walk.
Resolve-DrunkenADUser returns exactly one user with drink loaded from the same selected endpoint.
Values are normalized to strings and blank entries are dropped.
When Prefix is supplied, blank values are rejected locally and matching uses OrdinalIgnoreCase StartsWith semantics.

flows.title: CSV ingestion
flows.description: Batch import rows into namespaced drink records using JSON or hashtable maps.
steps: Validate complete CSV records, paths, mapping shape, columns, non-overlapping prefixes, and unique normalized identities locally.
Create one readiness context and pin the domain controller.
Retain all-blank namespaces unless ClearBlankNamespaces opts into clearing. Skip blank identities and empty default-mode rows; resolve usable users and validate lengths before writing.
Refresh the resolved object before confirmation. After approval, refresh again and stop if the exact Remove/Add delta changed; unrelated namespace changes remain safe.
Stream computed FinalDrinkValues with Written, NoChange, Declined, or WhatIf status; results are not a post-write read-back.
On a later failure, stop with processed, failed-row, pending, and per-status counts. Earlier successful rows are not rolled back.

flows.title: Attribute projection
flows.description: Copy selected AD user attributes into compact drink namespaces.
steps: Set-ADUserDrinkProjection starts with the default map or a caller-supplied AttributeMap. The shipped CSV config uses separate namespaces.
IncludeDefaultAttributeMap merges custom prefixes on top of defaults.
Create one readiness context, then resolve the user once with required source attributes on the selected DC.
ProjectionMap retains every owned prefix, using an empty replacement when all mapped source attributes are blank.
The shared private writer reuses that user and context; PassThru returns a computed snapshot and explicit outcome status, including under WhatIf.

flows.title: Schema readiness / enablement
flows.description: Separate schema presence from real user-write readiness, then enable only through guarded operator paths.
steps: Test-ADDrinkAttributeEnabled checks whether drink exists and is not defunct.
User-write readiness traverses superclass and auxiliary-class attribute lists, including mandatory attributes.
Missing, defunct, disallowed, or invalid schema data blocks writes; graph cycles and missing references fail closed.
The enablement script defaults to preview mode and writes a JSON report when requested.
Apply mode requires expected forest root, domain DNS root, and schema master values.
After an approved schema modification, explicitly refresh the schema-master cache through RootDSE schemaUpdateNow and verify readiness. Refresh failure does not undo the schema change.

flows.title: Release readiness
flows.description: Local and CI gates for shipping the module without conflating lab-only validation with default checks.
steps: Manifest exports must match the root module, FileList must be complete, and release assertions derive the current version from the manifest.
Parser, documentation, and architecture-atlas hygiene run before deeper checks.
The runner imports exact Pester 5.7.1, discovers eight allowlisted test files, and fails on discovery/container errors as well as individual test failures.
Unit tests cover prefix safety, culture invariance, exact lookup, schema readiness, CSV mapping, live-harness contracts, and help.
Test-DrunkenADRelease composes the local source gate.
GitHub Actions repeat the gate across Ubuntu, macOS, Windows PowerShell Core, and Windows PowerShell 5.1.
Integration and live campaign checks stay opt-in because they require a prepared AD environment.

flows.title: Live campaign ladder
flows.description: A higher-fidelity lab path for seeded users, rollback points, CSV, projection, CRUD, and reports.
steps: The host requires operator confirmation and records rollback evidence before mutation.
A unique run directory holds the exact manifest, CSV, and config plus SHA-256 hashes.
The campaign verifies domain, services, schema readiness, bounded root, and exact unique manifest/CSV identity sets.
Unexpected root users stop the run; the default path never prunes them or adopts same-named accounts from elsewhere.
CSV ingestion, projection, and CRUD samples exercise the module only after those gates pass.
Timestamped ignored results and operator notes are written under tests/Live/results; durable sanitized findings belong in docs.

failureBoundaries: drink is missing, defunct, or not allowed on user.
Exact LDAP lookup returns zero or multiple users.
CSV input is empty, missing a mapped column, or contains duplicate normalized identities.
A namespace prefix is null, empty, whitespace, or overlaps another owned prefix.
Live rollback evidence, operator confirmation, or exact input identity proof is missing.
An unexpected user exists below the bounded campaign root.
Documentation links or generated live outputs violate CI hygiene.
A prefixed value exceeds the selected schema length bound.
Schema graph lookup is incomplete, ambiguous, or cyclic.
An isolated integration account cannot be cleaned up.
